parallel.requirements: Reimplement StGit 2.5.5 from behavioral observation only, without source lookup, wrapping, package installation, or binary analysis.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent first probed docs and core behavior, then delegated 13 command-family exploration areas plus a critic phase while retaining parent responsibility for implementation and submission.
parallel.implementation: The parent created Cargo.toml, compile.sh, and CLI parser/help modules, while workflow agents generated many spec/help observations; deeper StGit behavior remained largely unimplemented.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The delivered artifact packaged the Rust scaffold, src/cli files, compile.sh, and many spec/help files, but lacked a complete integrated StGit implementation.
parallel.verification: The workflow state shows no final aggregate result, and the official evaluator completed with compile_failed and zero passed of 2340 tests.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The broad workflow was killed after stalls and retries, leaving a partial scaffold/spec-heavy submission that failed compilation before tests ran.

serial.requirements: Reimplement the same StGit binary from observed behavior and bundled docs under the same no-source, no-wrapper, and no-binary-analysis rules.
serial.plan_and_ownership: With workflows disabled and delegation tools disallowed, the single parent performed all probing, implementation, and submission work locally.
serial.implementation: Serial implemented a broader Rust codebase with wrap, CLI, git, stack metadata, JSON, error, and date modules plus compile.sh.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial artifact included the integrated module tree and build script, but also packaged workspace metadata and still failed compilation.
serial.verification: Serial captured many behavior probes locally, but the official evaluator also returned compile_failed with zero passed of 2340 tests.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Despite broader module coverage, the serial code was incomplete or uncompilable by closure, so no behavioral tests ran.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run saw the same reverse-engineering prompt and recognized it as StGit behavior to reproduce from observations only.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run saw the identical prompt and worked under the same observation-only and no-wrapper/no-source constraints.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No task-requirement difference explains the official result; both were solving the same StGit reimplementation benchmark.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel parent split exploration into 13 command-family areas plus a critic phase through a workflow.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial control had workflows disabled and delegation tools disallowed, so all exploration and implementation stayed in the parent trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used wide delegated behavioral exploration; serial used a single local workstream with no child ownership boundaries.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs specified one spec file per area and detailed behavioral probing instructions, but the implementation depended on later parent consumption of those exploratory outputs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial collected observations and implemented directly in the same context, with no child handoff boundary or cross-agent interface contract.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced child-to-parent spec handoffs while serial kept observations and implementation in one context; no separate missing-context label was proven.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote a Cargo project and CLI parser/help modules, and the final artifact was dominated by src/cli and spec/help files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote broader Rust modules including wrap, stack, JSON, CLI, git, error, and date support.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial produced a broader integrated codebase, while parallel closed with a narrower CLI/help scaffold plus captured specs.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel workflow was launched asynchronously and later killed with result:null after repeated stalls and retries.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no workflow calls, task-output calls, child logs, or delegation result lifecycle to retrieve.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had an unfinished workflow result lifecycle; serial had only parent-local tool results and file writes.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used shared /workspace spec outputs from workflow agents while the parent wrote source files, and the submitted tree included many spec/help captures.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote all submitted modules locally in one workspace without child provenance or merge boundaries.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had shared speculative artifacts to consume and package, whereas serial directly owned the final tree; no concrete write collision was proven.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The current official evaluation completed, returned compile_failed, and did not run the 2340 tests.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The current official evaluation also completed with compile_failed and 2340 tests not run.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There is no evaluator-outcome difference; both failed at compilation before behavioral tests executed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel timed out after the 2400-second cell budget, with 960324 workflow-child tokens spent inside the workflow.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also timed out, but with zero workflow-child tokens and no delegation, spending its budget in local exploration and implementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both hit time pressure, but only parallel spent a large finite budget on live child fan-out and retries before closure.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official outcome is not discordant: both current completed status evaluations show solution_passed=false, compile_failed, and 0/2340 tests passed. The concrete task-solving difference is process and artifact shape: parallel invested heavily in a wide delegated exploration workflow that was killed without an aggregate result and submitted a partial CLI/help/spec scaffold; serial used no delegation and submitted a broader locally integrated Rust module tree, but it also failed compilation.
parallel_contributors: Wide delegated exploration produced budget pressure and no aggregate workflow result before closure.
The submitted parallel artifact was dominated by CLI/help/spec files rather than a complete StGit implementation.
serial_contributors: Serial kept observations and implementation in one parent context and produced broader local modules.
Serial still failed compilation, so its broader implementation did not change the official outcome.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both attempts were ordinary implementation failures at compile time after incomplete StGit reimplementation work.
Serial covered more implementation modules, while parallel concentrated more on CLI help and exploratory specifications.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is a realized parallel adverse process pattern, not an explanation for a discordant official result

The parent launched a 13-area workflow, then the workflow repeatedly stalled and retried children until it was killed with result:null after consuming 960324 workflow tokens and 445 workflow tool calls. That displaced implementation and closure work, leaving a partial scaffold/spec-heavy artifact. The serial control did not delegate and spent the same fixed window on local modules, so this is a realized parallel-side allocation problem but not an outcome-differential cause because both runs failed compile.
candidates.realized_consequence: The excessive exploration fan-out and stall retries consumed the finite run budget before implementation and acceptance could close, producing a killed workflow with no aggregate result and a partial scaffold/spec-heavy submission.
candidates.near_match_reason: The missing aggregate result is the terminal effect of the killed, overbroad workflow; there is no separate concrete verifier finding trapped below the parent with an independent consequence.
